title: Opcode bridge spike amd64 measurement campaign

acceptedReview.implementationCorrectness: accepted by parent; no correctness blockers
acceptedReview.measurementHarness: Luna accepted actual Go helper/bridge required costs, fresh-process per-row resource isolation, and all 21 campaign commands
acceptedReview.acceptedP2: startup groups run in fixed order before seeded steady-state rows; startup is labeled as ordered observation, not randomized startup comparison; no harness changes were made for this interpretation limit
acceptedReview.measurementEvidence: Sol independently verified all 21 command results, 288 latency rows across three seeds, 180 serial benchmark repetitions, source/raw hashes, and calculations; no blockers.

methodology.latencyPercentiles: nearest-rank index ceil(p*N)-1 over individual synchronous request durations
methodology.closedLoopThroughput: completed calls divided by steady-state wall duration at caller concurrency; excludes startup, first request, preflight, warmup, GC setup, and close
methodology.comparisonMethod: same-seed, same-workload, same-concurrency candidate / Go helper; gate summary is median of the three paired run ratios; per-run results and pass counts retained
methodology.memoryComparison: aggregate sampled peak RSS candidate / Go helper; Go and FFI use host RSS; process uses host plus lane workers
methodology.startupInterpretation: Process startup groups cover only process lanes and include spawn through READY; FFI initialization is not measured as process startup, and FFI rows have no spawn/READY duration.

limitations: Startup groups run in fixed order before seeded steady-state rows and are ordered observations, not randomized comparisons; no cold-cache comparison was controlled.
Native arm64 execution and final GNU Cgo link/runtime check were not performed; no arm64 performance claim is made.
FFI hard cancellation is unavailable; CGO_ENABLED=0 process packaging versus FFI policy remains unresolved.
RSS is sampled every 10 ms; samples can miss short peaks, host RSS includes runtime/fixture allocation, sequential /proc reads are approximate, and summed process RSS double-counts shared pages.
Proposed thresholds remain uncalibrated and are shown as pass/fail outcomes without adjustment.
No FFI initialization duration is measured as process startup; the FFI first-request field is not a process-startup measurement.

Committed artifacts do not retain each row’s 10,000 individual request durations, so percentiles cannot be independently reconstructed from those artifacts; raw logs remain in local cache outside the repository.
Go B/op and allocs/op exclude allocations made inside the Rust allocator.

The host was unpinned and had elevated preflight load; three-run variance limits median-based route selection. The 8/16 full-response FFI median all-metrics pass count is not robust: only 2/16 cells pass all three metrics on every run.
